statement.name: Halpern–Läuchli theorem
statement.definition: For infinite leafless trees T_0..T_{d-1} and a k-coloring of the level products ⋃_n T_0(n)×…×T_{d-1}(n), there are strong subtrees with a common level function whose level product is monochromatic.
statement.facts: It is computably true (Theorem 3.4), its forest version is computably true (Theorem 3.6), and it admits strong cone avoidance (Theorem 3.21).

statement.name: Milliken's tree theorem for height 1
statement.definition: Milliken's tree theorem restricted to colorings of strong subtrees of height 1 (i.e. nodes).
statement.facts: It admits strong cone avoidance (Theorem 3.13).

statement.name: Product version of Milliken's tree theorem for height n
statement.definition: For d infinite leafless trees and a k-coloring of S_n(T_0,…,T_{d-1}), there is a tuple in S_ω(T_0,…,T_{d-1}) on which the coloring is constant.
statement.facts: Every X-computable instance has a Δ^{0,X}_{2n-1} solution (Theorem 4.6). It is provable in ACA0, and (∀n)PMTT^n is provable in ACA'_0 (Corollary 4.7). PMTT^n is equivalent to ACA0 for n≥3 and (∀n)PMTT^n is equivalent to ACA'_0 (Corollary 4.9). PMTT^2 admits cone avoidance and does not imply ACA0 (Theorem 4.15, Corollary 4.16).

statement.name: Product Milliken tree theorem with ℓ colors allowed in the solution
statement.definition: Like PMTT^n with k colors, but the solution may take at most ℓ colors.
statement.facts: PMTT^2_{k,2} admits strong cone avoidance (Theorem 4.27). (∀k)PMTT^3_{k,2} admits cone avoidance and does not imply ACA0 (Theorem 4.28, Corollary 4.29). It implies (∀k)JDT^2_{k,4} (Theorem 5.43).

statement.name: Ramsey's theorem with ℓ colors allowed in the solution
statement.definition: Every f:[N]^n→k has an infinite H such that f uses at most ℓ colors on [H]^n.
statement.facts: Strong cone avoidance of RT^2_{k,2} is cited from Wang and Cholak–Patey. RT^2_{k,ℓ} ≤_c DT^2_{2k,2ℓ+1} (Theorem 5.32). JRG^2_{4k,4n+3} implies RT^2_{k,n} (Theorem 6.41).

statement.name: Devlin's theorem
statement.definition: Every f:[Q]^n→k has a dense suborder S without endpoints with |f([S]^n)| ≤ ℓ.
statement.facts: There is a computable instance of DT^2_{4,3} all of whose solutions compute ∅' (Theorem 5.28), so DT^2_{4,3} implies ACA0 (Corollary 5.31). RT^2_{k,ℓ} ≤_c DT^2_{2k,2ℓ+1} (Theorem 5.32). (∀k)DT^2_{k,ℓ} has a computable instance whose solutions are all DNC relative to ∅'' and none of which is Σ^0_3 (Corollaries 5.39, 5.41). DT^2_{4,2} implies ER^2 (Theorem 5.48). DT^2_{<∞,4} (via JDT) admits cone avoidance and does not imply ACA0 (Corollaries 5.44, 5.45). Tight bounds are the odd tangent numbers (Corollary 5.26).

statement.name: Joyce Devlin's theorem
statement.definition: Devlin's theorem for DLO Joyce structures: there is a substructure copy on which f uses at most ℓ colors.
statement.facts: It is equivalent to DT for the same parameters (Corollary 5.25, Corollary 5.8). (∀k)PMTT^3_{k,2} implies (∀k)JDT^2_{k,4} (Theorem 5.43). (∀k)JDT^2_{k,4} admits cone avoidance (Corollary 5.44).

statement.name: Rado graph theorem
statement.definition: Every k-coloring of n-subsets (or of copies of G) of the Rado graph has a Rado subgraph on which at most ℓ colors appear.
statement.facts: (∀k)RG^2_{k,4} admits cone avoidance and does not imply ACA0 (Theorem 6.32, Corollary 6.40). For F of size 3 with b the number of Joyce types of F, (∀k)RG^F_{k,b} implies ACA0 (Corollary 6.48, Theorem 6.45, PA over ∅'). (∀k)RG^{K_3}_{k,16} and (∀k)RG^3_{k,112} imply ACA0 (Corollaries 6.49, 6.51). RG^2_{8,4} implies SRT^2_2 over RCA0 (Theorem 6.55). RT^2_2 does not imply (∀k)RG^2_{k,ℓ} for any ℓ (Theorem 6.63, via an ω-model).

statement.name: Joyce Rado graph theorem
statement.definition: Rado graph theorem for Joyce Rado graph structures.
statement.facts: Tight bound is the number of Joyce graphs (Corollary 6.27, ACA0). JRG^2_{4k,4n+3} implies RT^2_{k,n} and JRG^2_{8,7} implies RT^2_2 (Theorem 6.41). JRG^2_{2k,2n+1} implies DT^2_{k,n}, hence JRG^2_{8,7} implies ACA0 (Theorem 6.43). RG implies JRG over ACA0 (Corollary 6.29).

statement.name: (Strong) generalized Chubb–Hirst–McNicholl tree theorem
statement.definition: For f:[2^{<ω}]^n→k (all n-sets, not only chains) there is a perfect (resp. strong) subtree on which f uses at most ℓ colors.
statement.facts: (∀k)SCHMTT^n_{k,tsTT(n)} is provable in ACA0 and the bound is tight (Theorem 7.9). CHMTT^n_{k,tTT(n)} is provable in ACA0 and the bound is tight (Theorem 7.20).

statement.name: Proper PAC learning problem
statement.definition: Given a closed concept class C ⊆ 2^N (full, positive or negative information) and d ≥ VCdim(C), find a learner A:S→C and a sample complexity m with which A properly PAC learns C; the <d versions drop d from the input and assume VCdim(C) < d.
statement.facts: PPAC ≡sW PPAC_{<d} ≡sW ERM ≡sW id (computable). PPAC_{<∞} ≡W C_N and ≡sW id × C_N ≡sW lim_Δ. PPAC^± ≡sW PPAC^±_{<d} ≡sW lim. PPAC^+_{<∞} ≡sW lim. PPAC^-_{<∞} ≡sW lim × C_N'.

statement.name: Improper PAC learning problem
statement.definition: As PPAC, but the learner may output arbitrary hypotheses in 2^N.
statement.facts: IPAC and IPAC^- are computable. IPAC_{<∞} ≡W C_N. IPAC^+ ≡sW WIT^+. DNC* ≤sW IPAC^+_{<2} ≤sW IPAC^+ <W WKL. PA <W IPAC^+_{<2}, and IPAC^+_{<2} ≰W WWKL^(n). IPAC^+ is not Las Vegas computable. WKL ≤sW C_N' ∗ IPAC^+. DNC* × C_N ≤W IPAC^+_{<∞} ≤W C_R.

statement.name: Relative PAC learning problem
statement.definition: Given C ∈ A^+, H ∈ A^- with C ⊆ H and d ≥ VCdim(C), find a learner into H with a sample complexity that PAC learns C relative to H.
statement.facts: RPAC ≡sW RPAC_{<d} ≡sW RPAC_fix ≡sW WKL. RPAC_{<∞} ≡sW C_R.

statement.name: VC dimension problems
statement.definition: Compute the VC dimension (in N∞) of a closed class, or an upper bound on it.
statement.facts: VCdim ≡sW VCdim^+ ≡sW SORT. VCdim^- ≡sW SORT'. VCdim_{<∞} ≡sW C_N. VCdim^-_{<∞} ≡sW C_N'. BVCdim ≡sW B.

statement.name: Witness problem
statement.definition: Given a closed class C and d ≥ VCdim(C), find a k-witness function for C.
statement.facts: WIT^- is computable. ACC_n ≰*_W WIT^+ for every n ≥ 2. DNC* ≤sW WIT^+ ≤sW WKL.

statement.name: Finitary DNC problem
statement.definition: Given instances of ACC_k^ for all k ≥ 2, find some k and a solution of the k-th instance.
statement.facts: PA <W DNC*. DNC_N <W DNC*. DNC* ≰W WWKL^(n) for every n.

statement.name: Supremum, maximum, boundedness, discrete limit
statement.definition: Standard benchmark problems on sequences of natural numbers.
statement.facts: SORT ≡sW sup. SORT_{<∞} ≡sW max ≡sW C_N. B ≡W C_N ≡W lim_Δ ≡sW id × C_N. B <sW C_N <sW lim_Δ.

statement.name: Characteristic function of PAC learnability
statement.definition: Decide whether a closed concept class is PAC learnable.
statement.facts: χ_PL ≡sW χ_PL^+ ≡sW LPO'. χ_PL^- ≡sW LPO''.

statement.name: Weak 1-genericity problem
statement.definition: Given q, find p weakly 1-generic relative to q.
statement.facts: HYP ≤sW 1-WGEN and 1-WGEN ≤W HYP, so HYP ≡W 1-WGEN (strong equivalence open, Question 9.6); 1-WGEN ≤W COH.

statement.name: Low Basis Theorem problem
statement.definition: Given an infinite binary tree T, find a path p with p′ ≤T T′.
statement.facts: WKL <W LBT <W L; LPO ≰W LBT; LBT |W C_R; LBT is discriminative.

statement.name: Kleene–Post theorem problem
statement.definition: Given r, find ⟨p,q⟩ with r ≤T ⟨p,q⟩ and p |T q.
statement.facts: KPT ≤sW MLR and KPT ≤sW 1-GEN, both strict.

statement.name: Friedberg jump inversion theorem; inverse of the Turing jump on degrees
statement.definition: JIT : D ⇒ D, a ↦ {b : b′ = a ∪ 0′}; J_D^{-1} is its restriction to the cone above 0′.
statement.facts: J_D^{-1} <sW JIT <sW c_∅′ × id; JIT ≤sW lim_J (strict); J_D^{-1} is not computable; JIT is continuous and limit computable but not computable; J_D^{-1} ∗s J_D^{-1} ≡sW 0; JIT ∗ JIT ≤W c_∅′ ≤W lim.

statement.name: Diagonally non-computable functions with k values; WKL for big k-branching trees; all-or-co-unique choice on n
statement.definition: DNC_X(p) = {q ∈ X^N : q(n) ≠ φ^p_n(n) for all n}; WKL_k finds paths in big trees in k*; ACC_n is choice on n with at most one element missing.
statement.facts: DNC_k ≡sW WKL_k ≡sW \hat{ACC_k}; ACC_n ≰W DNC_{n+1}; DNC_N <W DNC_{n+1} <W DNC_n; DNC_n is indiscriminative for n ≥ 3; DNC_2 ≤W C_N′ ∗ DNC_k; DNC_n is not probabilistic; MLR |W DNC_3; WKL_n |W (k−1)/k-WWKL for n ≥ 3, k ≥ 2.

statement.name: Quantitative weak weak König's lemma variants
statement.definition: ε-WWKL finds a path in a tree of measure > ε; (1−∗)-WWKL: given (T_n) with µ[T_n] > 1 − 2^{−n}, find a path in some T_n.
statement.facts: MLR <sW (1−∗)-WWKL; ACC_N <sW (1−∗)-WWKL; (1−∗)-WWKL is strongly parallelizable; DNC_N <sW (1−∗)-WWKL; ACC_{n+1} ≤sW (n−1)/n-WWKL and ACC_n ≰W (n−1)/n-WWKL; ε-WWKL is not parallelizable for ε ∈ [0,1).

statement.notation: lim_J, L, L_2, J_D, c_∅′ × id
statement.name: Restricted limit, low map, low2 map, Turing jump on degrees, constant halting problem
statement.definition: lim_J is lim restricted to sequences whose jumps converge; L = J^{-1}∘lim; L_2 = J^{-1}∘J^{-1}∘lim∘lim; J_D(a) = a′.
statement.facts: DNC_N ≰W lim_J; MLR ≰W lim_J; C_N ≤W lim_J; LBT ≤sW L; COH ≤sW L_2 and COH ≰sW L; WBWT_R ≤sW L_2 and WBWT_R ≰sW L; lim ∗s lim^{-1} ≡sW c_∅′ × id.

statement.name: Cohesiveness for enumerated sequences
statement.definition: COH with the sets R_i given by positive information (enumerations).
statement.facts: COH ≤sW COH+ ≤sW COH′; COH+ ≰W COH; 1-GEN ≰W COH+; ACC_N ≰W COH+; COH+ ≤sW lim′.

statement.name: Degree versions of problems
statement.facts: [COH] ≡sW J_D^{-1} ∘ PA ∘ J_D; [COH] ≤sW PA′; [COH] ≡W (lim → PA′) ≡W (JD → PA′) ≡W (lim → [WKL]′).

statement.name: Weak and subsequential Bolzano–Weierstraß theorems
statement.definition: WBWT_X outputs a sequence converging to a name of a cluster point; SBWT_X outputs a strictly monotone s with (x_{s(n)}) convergent.
statement.facts: WBWT_R is densely realized (ω-indiscriminative); WBWT_X ≡W (lim → BWT_X); WBWT_X ≡W SBWT_X; SBWT_{2^N} ≡sW SBWT_R ≡sW SBWT_[0,1] ≡sW SBWT_{[0,1]^N}; SBWT_R ≡sW COH; COH ≡W \hat{WBWT_2}; BWT_R ≡W lim ∗ WBWT_R; WBWT_R is low2 but not low.
